name: vcell-hybrid-paper-benchmarks
title: Reproducing the VCell hybrid methods paper (Schaff et al. 2016) with the native solver and the co-simulation

at_a_glance.role: Test 1 / Fig 1, error vs number of trials and time step against the analytic expectation.
Tests 2 / Figs 2-3, distributions p(U,t) and P(n,t) against a Gibson-Bruck SSA in the fast-diffusion limit.
Tests 3-5 / Figs 4-6, single-channel densities against direct Fokker-Planck solutions.
Test 6 / Fig 7, relaxation and t^-3/2 tail; documents the point-particle limitation.
Stretch goal, Test 7 / Fig 8, membrane receptor clustering (needs membrane particles).

question: Do VCell's native PDE/particle hybrid solver (vcell-fvsolver with embedded Smoldyn) and the process-bigraph co-simulation both reproduce the validation results of Schaff et al. (2016, PLoS Comput Biol 12:e1005236), and where do they differ?
hypothesis: On the paper's calcium-spark benchmarks, both solvers match the analytic, Gibson-Bruck and Fokker-Planck references to within the paper's reported accuracy (L2 about 1-3% of maximum, statistical error proportional to N^-1/2). Residual differences between the two solvers come from the Smoldyn version (2.38 vs 2.7x) and coupling details, which are measurable.

executive.what_is_this: A reproduction of the published validation of VCell's hybrid solver, used both to validate the headless native reference path and to benchmark the co-simulation on established cases.

studies.name: separable-calcium-sparks
studies.title: Schaff et al. 2016, Test 1 / Fig 1B: separable calcium sparks on both solvers
studies.question:
Do the native VCell hybrid solver and the process-bigraph co-simulation both reproduce
Fig 1B of Schaff et al. (2016)? The error of the trial-mean calcium against its exact
expectation should fall as N^-1/2 with the number of trials, and be statistically
dominated at small Δt.

studies.name: coupled-sparks-fast-diffusion
studies.title: Schaff et al. 2016, Test 2 / Fig 2: coupled calcium sparks in the fast-diffusion limit, both solvers
studies.question:
With channel opening coupled to local calcium (k_on·U(rᵢ)/U₀) and fast diffusion
(D = 1000 µm²/s), do both hybrid solvers reproduce the distributions of calcium and
open-channel number given by the exact well-mixed process, as in Fig 2 of the paper?
